title: QUIZ - 97
description: Test your knowledge, strengthen your reasoning, and learn something new with every question.

questions.concept: Explaining Why a Sentence Is Not a Statement
questions.learningObjective: Explain the specific reason a given sentence fails to be a logical statement
questions.question: Why is "y is greater than 10." NOT considered a logical statement?

options.label: A
options.text: It is a command, which cannot be assigned a truth value.

options.label: B
options.text: It is a question, which cannot be assigned a truth value.

options.label: C
options.text: It refers to its own truth value, creating a paradox rather than a fixed truth value.

options.label: D
options.text: It contains a variable with an unknown value, so its truth cannot be determined.

questions.explanation: "y is greater than 10." fails to be a statement because it contains a variable with an unknown value, so its truth cannot be determined.
questions.hint: Consider whether the sentence is a question, a command, self-referential, an exclamation, or contains an undetermined variable.

questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a given sentence qualifies as a logical statement
questions.question: Is the sentence "How old are you?" a logical statement?

options.label: A
options.text: This cannot be determined without more context.

options.label: B
options.text: No, it is not a statement.

options.label: C
options.text: It is a statement only some of the time.

options.label: D
options.text: Yes, it is a statement.

questions.explanation: "How old are you?" is not a statement because it is a question, command, exclamation, or contains an unknown variable, so it has no fixed truth value.
questions.hint: A statement must be a declarative sentence that can be judged true or false; questions, commands, and sentences with unknown variables are not statements.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize that an equation with an unassigned variable is not a statement until the variable's value is known
questions.question: Is the open sentence "y + 12 = 24" a logical statement in the strict sense (without knowing the value of y)?

options.label: A
options.text: No, because its truth depends on the unknown value of y.

options.label: B
options.text: Yes, because it contains an equals sign.

options.label: C
options.text: No, because equations can never be statements.

options.label: D
options.text: Yes, because y is always equal to 12.

questions.explanation: An open sentence like "y + 12 = 24" only becomes a true or false statement once a specific value is substituted for y; without that, its truth value is undetermined.
questions.hint: A sentence containing an unassigned variable is an 'open sentence,' not a statement, until a value is substituted.
